newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: British Airways in deal with Swiss airline.
newsitem.headline: British Airways in deal with Swiss airline.

text.p: British Airways has won a technical contract to service the fleet of Swiss World Airways, Geneva's new airline for French-speaking Switzerland, Swiss news agency ATS quoted a BA statement as saying.

Under the five-year contract, British Airways will handle the maintenance of leased aircraft SWA hopes to use to start transatlantic flights later this year from its home base in Geneva, ATS said. It did not give the size of the contract.
Boeing said on Tuesday that it won an order worth $203 million from SWA for two 767-300 extended range 210-seat widebody twinjets for delivery in the third quarter of 1998.
SWA hopes to fly from Geneva's Cointrin airport, which serves western Switzerland and Alpine France, to destinations such as New York, Washington, Boston, Chicago and Montreal.
It was created after nationaal carrier Swissair stopped most of its loss-making long-haul flights from Geneva in favour of the Zurich hub last year.

SWA will have a start-up capital of 60 million Swiss francs. The airline is seeking financial guarantees of between 15 million and 20 million Swiss francs from cantonal governments in French-speaking Switzerland that are backing it.
